summary: The study describes the deposition of ultrathin alumina and titania films on porous poly(styrene-divinylbenzene) (PS-DVB) particles using atomic layer deposition (ALD) at low temperatures. The films were used to enhance the bioactivity of the polymer substrates by promoting the formation of hydroxyapatite (HA) in simulated body fluid (SBF). The ALD process was found to create conformal ceramic films on both internal and external polymer surfaces, which facilitated HA formation and cell adhesion.
evidence: Alumina and titania films were deposited by alternating reactions of trimethylaluminum and H2O at 33 °C and of titanium tetrachloride and H2O2 at 100 °C, respectively. The improved bioactivity of the polymer substrates was revealed on the basis of the formation of hydroxyapatite (HA) in simulated body fluid. The accelerated formation of HA on the ALD-modified polymer surface was caused by the negatively charged surface provided by the ultrathin ceramic interface.
